paragraph_text: The Beneficiary satisfies 8 C.F.R. §204.5(h)(3)(i) by demonstrating receipt of nationally and internationally recognized awards for excellence in the field. The Beneficiary was selected as a scholar of Beijing's 'Hundred People Project,' a prestigious talent recognition program that identifies and supports exceptional academics in the capital region [Exhibit A1, p.2]. This selection demonstrates that the Beneficiary's scholarly work has been recognized at the highest levels of academic administration in Beijing, as the program is designed to identify and cultivate leading researchers who contribute to the region's intellectual capital [Exhibit A1, p.2]. The 'Hundred People Project' represents a highly competitive selection process, as evidenced by its name which implies selection from a much larger pool of qualified candidates, making the Beneficiary's inclusion a significant honor that reflects his standing among his academic peers [Exhibit A1, p.2]. Furthermore, the Beneficiary's work 'On Age' won the third prize of Outstanding Achievements in Humanities and Social Sciences of the Ministry of Education of China, a nationally recognized award established by the Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China in 2009 [Exhibit A1, p.2; Exhibit B10, p.2, p.4]. This award is administered through a rigorous three-year selection cycle and includes multiple categories such as books, papers, and research reports, with all awards divided into grand prizes, first prizes, second prizes, and third prizes [Exhibit B10, p.4, p.5]. The evaluation process involves an Award Committee composed of the director and deputy directors of the Social Sciences Committee of the Ministry of Education, along with heads of relevant departments, and employs experts and scholars with high academic attainments from across the country to conduct independent evaluations [Exhibit B10, p.5]. While the Beneficiary received the third prize, this represents a significant achievement within a four-tier award structure where only the most exceptional works receive recognition at any level, demonstrating that his work was selected from a national pool of submissions and deemed worthy of ministerial recognition [Exhibit B10, p.5]. In addition to these academic honors, the Beneficiary received the Data Legacy of the Year Award at the 2019 Data Awards, which are pronounced the same as 'beacon' in Chinese and represent one of the most influential awards in the field of mobile Internet [Exhibit B1, p.2; Exhibit B3, p.2, p.3]. These awards were jointly launched by Umen+, Zhongguancun Big Data Industry Alliance, Tsingdata Big Data Industries Association, and China Big Data Industry Observation, with a jury of 21 judges from dozens of authorities and industry experts including China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, Tsinghua University, and Peking University [Exhibit B3, p.3]. Through the development of professional selection models, only 28 Data individuals stood out from what was undoubtedly a much larger pool of candidates, with the Beneficiary recognized in the Data Legacy of the Year category for those who have worked deeply in big data and mobile Internet for many years, spreading insights and experiences while educating the entire industry [Exhibit B3, p.4, p.7]. The Data Awards also included other prestigious categories such as Most Influential Award of the Year and Best Data Practice Award of the Year, with recipients described as veterans in mobile Internet and leaders in data intelligence who drive business practice through years of data accumulation [Exhibit B3, p.6, p.8]. Moreover, the Beneficiary, along with co-author Chen Cui, won the Excellent Paper Award at the 11th China Communication Conference for their paper titled 'Challenges Posed by the Internet to Traditional Media in the Time Dimension - A Study on the Possibility of Internet Media Usage Time Surpassing Traditional Media Usage Time' [Exhibit B11, p.2]. This award was issued by the Communication Association of China through the 11th China Communication Conference Organizing Committee, representing recognition from the premier professional organization for communication studies in China [Exhibit B11, p.2]. The China Communication Conference represents a major national gathering of communication scholars and professionals, making the Excellent Paper Award a competitive honor that recognizes outstanding research contributions within this important academic community [Exhibit B11, p.2]. Beyond these individual recognitions, the Beneficiary's recognition extends to multiple industry sectors, as evidenced by Umen+'s receipt of numerous prestigious awards including Enterprise Service High-growth Company 36 Kr and China Big Data Industry Application TOP Choice Three Major Fields, demonstrating the caliber of organizations with which the Beneficiary is associated [Exhibit B4, p.4]. These industry recognitions include awards from established institutions such as the Data Technology Industry Innovation Institute (DTiii), which named Umen+ to the 2019 China Big Data Innovative Enterprises TOP 100 list, and the Chaoyang Public Security Branch Network Security Guarding Brigade, which awarded Umen+ the 2018 Excellent Team Award of Internet Security Management [Exhibit B4, p.4]. The breadth of these awards across enterprise service, big data innovation, internet security, and retail technology sectors demonstrates that the Beneficiary operates within organizations that are consistently recognized as leaders across multiple domains of technology and business application [Exhibit B4, p.4]. In sum, the foregoing evidence clearly establishes that the Beneficiary has received nationally and internationally recognized awards for excellence in the field.
